name: Visualization Checklist
description: This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any visualization task, implementation, or piece of work complete.
content:
This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any visualization task, implementation, or piece of work complete.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Before starting visualization work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
2. Prefer the simplest visualization approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
3. Check that visualization terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
4. Document any non-obvious visualization decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
5. Measure before optimizing any visualization bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
6. Keep visualization outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
7. When visualization decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
8. When multiple visualization strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
9. Re-check edge cases relevant to visualization (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
10. Prefer explicit, readable visualization solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
11. Surface known limitations of a chosen visualization approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop visualization edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not skip documenting visualization assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid introducing new visualization abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for visualization, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
